name: Django ORM raw-SQL escape hatch (extra/RawSQL)
attack_scenario: A request supplies name = "x' OR '1'='1' -- "; the extra()/RawSQL fragment closes the literal and appends attacker SQL, turning a filtered lookup into a full-table read or auth bypass under the DB user's privileges.
negative_test_hint: submit name = "' OR '1'='1' -- " and assert the query returns a single row or errors, not the whole table

exemplar.explanation: Django's QuerySet.extra() and RawSQL() drop out of the ORM's parameter binding; building their SQL fragments with f-strings, %, +, or .format() splices user input straight into the query. Both APIs accept a params= list precisely so values never touch the SQL text, so the %s-placeholder-plus-params form (where=["price > %s"], params=[minp]) is safe and is NOT flagged. Only interpolation into the fragment matches. .extra() is deprecated for exactly this reason.
